verses.1:1: How she sits alone, the city great in people! She has become like a widow; great among the nations, a princess among the provinces, she has become subject to forced labor.
verses.1:2: Bitterly she weeps in the night, and her tears are upon her cheek. She has no comforter among all her lovers; all her companions have acted treacherously against her; they have become her enemies.
verses.1:3: Judah has gone into exile because of affliction and heavy servitude; she dwells among the nations and finds no resting place. All her pursuers have overtaken her in the narrow straits.
verses.1:4: Zion's roads mourn, with no one coming to the appointed festival. All her gates lie desolate; her priests groan, her virgins are grieved, and she herself is in bitterness.
verses.1:5: Her adversaries have become the head; her enemies are at ease, for the LORD has afflicted her because of the multitude of her transgressions. Her little children have gone into captivity before the adversary.
verses.1:6: From the daughter of Zion all her splendor has departed. Her princes have become like stags that find no pasture, and they have gone without strength before the pursuer.
verses.1:7: Jerusalem remembers, in the days of her affliction and wandering, all her precious things that were from days of old. When her people fell into the hand of an adversary and there was no helper for her, the adversaries saw her and mocked at her collapse.
verses.1:8: Jerusalem has sinned severely; therefore she has become an object of scorn. All who honored her hold her in contempt, because they have seen her nakedness; she herself also groans and turns away.
verses.1:9: Her uncleanness is in her skirts; she did not consider her end. So she came down astonishingly; there is no comforter for her. "See, LORD, my affliction, for the enemy has magnified himself!"
verses.1:10: Over all her precious things the adversary has spread out his hand; indeed, she has seen nations enter her sanctuary, those whom You commanded that they should not enter Your assembly.
verses.1:11: All her people groan as they seek bread; they have given their precious things for food to restore life. "See, LORD, and look, for I have become contemptible!
verses.1:12: Is it nothing to you, all who pass along the road? Look and see whether there is any anguish like my anguish, which has been dealt to me, with which the LORD has afflicted me on the day of His burning anger.
verses.1:13: From on high He sent fire into my bones, and it mastered them; He spread a net for my feet and turned me back. He has made me desolate, faint all the day.
verses.1:14: The yoke of my transgressions was fastened by His hand; they were intertwined and came up upon my neck. He has caused my strength to fail; the Lord has given me into the hands of those against whom I cannot rise.
verses.1:15: The Lord has spurned all my mighty men in my midst; He has summoned an appointed assembly against me to shatter my young men. As in a winepress, the Lord has trodden the virgin daughter of Judah.
verses.1:16: Because of these things I weep; my eye, my eye streams with water, for far from me is a comforter, one who restores my life. My children have become desolate, for the enemy has prevailed."
verses.1:17: Zion spreads out her hands, yet there is no comforter for her. The LORD has commanded concerning Jacob that those around him should be his adversaries; Jerusalem has become an unclean thing among them.
verses.1:18: "The LORD is righteous, for I have rebelled against His command. Listen, please, all the peoples, and see my anguish: my virgins and my young men have gone into captivity.
verses.1:19: I called to my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and my elders perished in the city while they sought food for themselves to restore their life.
verses.1:20: See, LORD, for I am in distress; my inward parts are in turmoil. My heart is overturned within me, for I have utterly rebelled. Outside, the sword bereaves; inside the house, it is like death.
verses.1:21: They have heard that I groan; there is no comforter for me. All my enemies have heard of my calamity; they rejoice that You have done it. You have brought the day You proclaimed; let them become like me!
verses.1:22: Let all their wickedness come before You, and deal with them just as You have dealt with me because of all my transgressions; for my groanings are many, and my heart is faint."
verses.2:1: How the Lord in His anger has shrouded the daughter of Zion in a cloud! He has hurled from heaven to earth the glory of Israel, and He did not remember His footstool on the day of His anger.
verses.2:2: The Lord has swallowed up all the dwellings of Jacob and did not spare them; in His fury He has torn down the strongholds of the daughter of Judah. He has brought them down to the ground; He has profaned the kingdom and its princes.
verses.2:3: In burning anger He has cut off every horn of Israel; He has drawn back His right hand from before the enemy. He has burned in Jacob like a flaming fire that devours on every side.
verses.2:4: He has bent His bow like an enemy, with His right hand poised like an adversary, and He has killed all who were precious to the eye. In the tent of the daughter of Zion He has poured out His wrath like fire.
verses.2:5: The Lord has become like an enemy; He has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all its citadels and destroyed its strongholds, and He has multiplied mourning and lamentation in the daughter of Judah.
verses.2:6: He has ravaged His booth like a garden; He has destroyed His appointed meeting place. The LORD has caused appointed festival and Sabbath to be forgotten in Zion, and in the indignation of His anger He has spurned king and priest.
verses.2:7: The Lord has rejected His altar and repudiated His sanctuary; He has delivered into the hand of the enemy the walls of her citadels. They raised a clamor in the house of the LORD as on the day of an appointed festival.
verses.2:8: The LORD planned to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion; He stretched out a measuring line and did not draw back His hand from swallowing up. He caused rampart and wall to mourn; together they languish.
verses.2:9: Her gates have sunk into the ground; He has ruined and shattered her bars. Her king and her princes are among the nations; there is no law, and her prophets also find no vision from the LORD.
verses.2:10: The elders of the daughter of Zion sit on the ground and keep silent; they have thrown dust on their heads and wrapped themselves in sackcloth. The virgins of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground.
verses.2:11: My eyes are spent with tears; my inward parts are in turmoil. My liver is poured out to the ground over the ruin of the daughter of my people, as little child and nursing infant grow faint in the squares of the city.
verses.2:12: To their mothers they say, "Where are grain and wine?" as they grow faint like the wounded in the squares of the city, as their life is poured out into their mothers' bosom.
verses.2:13: What can I testify for you? What can I liken to you, daughter of Jerusalem? What can I compare to you, so that I may comfort you, virgin daughter of Zion? For your ruin is as vast as the sea; who can heal you?
verses.2:14: Your prophets have seen for you falsehood and folly; they have not exposed your iniquity so as to restore your fortunes, but have seen for you false and misleading oracles.
verses.2:15: All who pass along the road clap their hands at you; they hiss and shake their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem: "Is this the city of which they say, 'The perfection of beauty, joy of all the earth'?"
verses.2:16: All your enemies open their mouths wide against you; they hiss and gnash their teeth. They say, "We have swallowed her up! Surely this is the day we waited for; we have found it, we have seen it!"
verses.2:17: The LORD has done what He purposed; He has carried out His word which He commanded from days of old. He has torn down and did not spare; He has made the enemy rejoice over you and exalted the horn of your adversaries.
verses.2:18: Their heart cried out to the Lord. Wall of the daughter of Zion, let tears stream down like a torrent day and night; give yourself no respite, and do not let the pupil of your eye rest.
verses.2:19: Arise, cry aloud in the night, at the beginning of the watches! Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord; lift up your hands to Him for the lives of your little children, who faint from hunger at the head of every street.
verses.2:20: "See, LORD, and look! With whom have You dealt like this? Should women eat their own fruit, the little children of their tender care? Should priest and prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
verses.2:21: Young and old lie on the ground in the streets; my virgins and my young men have fallen by the sword. You have killed them on the day of Your anger; You have slaughtered and did not spare.
verses.2:22: You summoned, as on the day of an appointed festival, my terrors on every side; and on the day of the LORD's anger there was no fugitive or survivor. Those whom I tenderly cared for and raised, my enemy has annihilated."
verses.3:1: I am the man who has seen affliction by the rod of His fury.
verses.3:2: He has driven me and led me into darkness, and not light.
verses.3:3: Indeed, against me He repeatedly turns His hand all day long.
verses.3:4: He has worn out my flesh and my skin; He has broken my bones in pieces.
verses.3:5: He has built against me and encircled me with poison and hardship.
verses.3:6: He has made me sit in dark places, like those long since dead.
verses.3:7: He has walled me in, and I cannot leave; He has made my bronze shackles heavy.
verses.3:8: Even though I cry out and call for help, He blocks my prayer.
verses.3:9: He has walled up my ways with cut stone; He has twisted my paths.
verses.3:10: He is to me a bear waiting in ambush, a lion in hiding places.
verses.3:11: He has diverted my ways and ripped me apart; He has left me desolate.
verses.3:12: He has bent His bow and stationed me as a target for the arrow.
verses.3:13: He has caused the sons of His quiver to enter my kidneys.
verses.3:14: I have become an object of laughter to all my people, their song all day long.
verses.3:15: He has sated me with bitter herbs; He has made me drink my fill of wormwood.
verses.3:16: And He has crushed my teeth with gravel; He has pressed me down into the ashes.
verses.3:17: And You have rejected my soul from peace; I have forgotten what is good.
verses.3:18: So I said, "My endurance and my hope from the LORD have perished."
verses.3:19: Remember my affliction and my homelessness, wormwood and poison.
verses.3:20: My soul surely remembers and sinks down within me.
verses.3:21: This I bring back to my heart; therefore I will hope.
verses.3:25: The LORD is good to those waiting for Him, to a soul that seeks Him.
verses.3:26: It is good to wait in silence for the deliverance of the LORD.
verses.3:27: It is good for a man to carry a yoke in his youth.
verses.3:28: Let him sit alone and keep silent, because He has imposed it upon him.
verses.3:30: Let him give his cheek to the one striking him; let him have his fill of reproach.
verses.3:31: For the Lord will not reject for all time.
verses.3:32: For though He brings grief, He will show compassion according to the abundance of His acts of loyal love.
verses.3:33: For it is not from His heart that He afflicts or brings grief to the sons of man.
verses.3:34: To crush under one's feet all the prisoners of the earth,
verses.3:35: to pervert a man's justice before the face of the Most High,
verses.3:36: to wrong a person in his case—the Lord does not approve.
verses.3:37: Who is this who has spoken and it came to be, if the Lord has not commanded it?
verses.3:38: Do not calamities and good come from the mouth of the Most High?
verses.3:39: Why should a living person complain, a man about his sins?
verses.3:40: Let us search our ways and probe them, and let us turn back to the LORD.
verses.3:41: Let us lift up our heart together with our hands to God in the heavens.
verses.3:42: We ourselves have transgressed and rebelled; You have not forgiven.
verses.3:43: You have shrouded Yourself in anger and pursued us. You have killed; You have not spared.
verses.3:44: You have shrouded Yourself in a cloud so that prayer cannot pass through.
verses.3:45: You make us sweepings and refuse in the midst of the peoples.
verses.3:46: All our enemies have opened their mouths wide at us.
verses.3:47: Terror and pitfall have fallen to us, desolation and ruin.
verses.3:48: My eye flows down with streams of water over the ruin of the daughter of my people.
verses.3:49: My eye pours out and will not cease, with no pause,
verses.3:50: until the LORD gazes down from the heavens and sees.
verses.3:51: My eye torments my soul because of all the daughters of my city.
verses.3:52: My enemies relentlessly hunted me like a bird, without cause.
verses.3:53: They silenced my life in the pit and hurled a stone at me.
verses.3:54: Waters flooded over my head; I said, "I have been cut off."
verses.3:55: I called out Your name, LORD, from the deepest pit.
verses.3:56: You heard my voice; do not hide Your ear from my gasping, from my cry for help.
verses.3:57: You drew near on the day I called to You; You said, "Do not be afraid."
verses.3:58: Lord, You pleaded the cases of my soul; You redeemed my life.
verses.3:59: LORD, You have seen the injustice done to me; judge my cause.
verses.3:60: You have seen all their vengefulness, all their plans against me.
verses.3:61: LORD, You have heard their reproach, all their plans against me.
verses.3:62: The lips of those who rise against me and their muttering are against me all day long.
verses.3:63: Look at their sitting down and their rising up; I am their taunt song.
verses.3:64: You will pay recompense to them, LORD, in accordance with the work of their hands.
verses.3:65: You will give them obstinacy of heart, Your curse upon them.
verses.3:66: You will pursue them in anger and wipe them out from beneath the heavens of the LORD.
verses.4:1: How gold has darkened, how the choice fine gold has changed! Holy stones are poured out at the head of all the streets.
verses.4:2: Zion's precious sons, valued against refined gold, how they are counted as clay jars, the work of the hands of a potter!
verses.4:3: Even jackals bare the breast; they nurse their cubs. Yet the daughter of my people has turned cruel, like ostriches in the wilderness.
verses.4:4: The tongue of a nursing infant clings to his palate from thirst; young children beg for bread, yet there is no one breaking it for them.
verses.4:5: Those who fed on delicacies lie desolate in the streets; those nurtured on crimson embrace refuse heaps.
verses.4:6: And the iniquity of the daughter of my people became greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in an instant, and no hands fell upon her.
verses.4:7: Her nobles were brighter than snow, whiter than milk; they were ruddier in frame than corals—their form was lapis lazuli.
verses.4:8: Their appearance has turned darker than soot; they go unrecognized in the streets. Their skin has drawn tight over their bones; it has dried up, it has become like wood.
verses.4:9: Better off were those killed by the sword than those killed by famine, for these drain away, pierced through for lack of the yield of the field.
verses.4:10: The hands of compassionate women cooked their children; they became food for them in the shattering of the daughter of my people.
verses.4:11: The LORD exhausted His wrath; He poured out His burning anger, and He kindled a fire in Zion, and it devoured her foundations.
verses.4:12: The kings of the earth, all who dwell in the world, did not believe that adversary and enemy would enter the gates of Jerusalem.
verses.4:13: On account of the sins of her prophets, the iniquities of her priests, who shed the blood of the righteous within her.
verses.4:14: Blind, they wandered in the streets; they were polluted with blood, so that no one could touch their clothing.
verses.4:15: "Turn aside! Unclean!" people called out to them, "Turn aside, turn aside, do not touch!" When they fled and also wandered, people said among the nations, "They will no longer sojourn."
verses.4:16: The face of the LORD has scattered them; He will no longer look upon them. They showed no honor to priests, and they showed no favor to elders.
verses.4:17: Still our eyes fail for our futile help; from our watchtower we have watched for a nation that cannot save.
verses.4:18: They stalked our steps so that we could not walk in our public squares; our end approached, our days were complete, for our end had come.
verses.4:19: Swifter were our pursuers than the eagles of the heavens; on the mountains they hotly pursued us, in the wilderness they lay in ambush for us.
verses.4:20: The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the LORD, was caught in their pits—the one about whom we said, "In his shadow we will live among the nations."
verses.4:21: Exult and be glad, daughter of Edom, who dwells in the land of Uz; even to you the cup will pass—you will grow drunk and strip yourself naked.
verses.4:22: The penalty for your iniquity has ended, daughter of Zion; He will not send you into exile again. He will call your iniquity to account, daughter of Edom; He will lay bare your sins.
verses.5:1: Remember, LORD, what has become of us; look closely and see our disgrace.
verses.5:2: Our inheritance has been turned over to outsiders, our houses to foreigners.
verses.5:3: We have become orphans and are without a father; our mothers are like widows.
verses.5:4: We drink our water for silver; our wood comes at a price.
verses.5:5: At our necks we are pursued; we have grown weary, and no rest is given to us.
verses.5:6: To Egypt we gave our hand, to Assyria, to be satisfied with bread.
verses.5:7: Our fathers sinned, and they are gone; yet we have borne their iniquities.
verses.5:8: Slaves have ruled over us; there is no rescuer from their hand.
verses.5:9: At the risk of our lives we bring in our bread, because of the sword of the wilderness.
verses.5:10: Our skin is scorched like an oven because of the raging heat of famine.
verses.5:11: Women in Zion they violated, virgins in the cities of Judah.
verses.5:12: Princes were hanged by their hands; the faces of elders were not honored.
verses.5:13: Young men carried the handmill, and boys stumbled under the wood.
verses.5:14: Elders have ceased from the gate, young men from their music.
verses.5:15: The gladness of our heart has ceased; our dancing has turned into mourning.
verses.5:16: The crown of our head has fallen; woe now to us, for we have sinned!
verses.5:17: Over this our heart has become faint; over these things our eyes have darkened.
verses.5:18: Over Mount Zion, which lies desolate—foxes walk about on it.
verses.5:19: You, LORD, sit enthroned forever; Your throne is for generation after generation.
verses.5:20: Why do You permanently forget us, why do You abandon us for so long a time?
verses.5:21: Bring us back to Yourself, LORD, that we may return; renew our days as in former times.
verses.5:22: Unless You have completely rejected us and are furious with us to the utmost.

notes.1:8: MT vocalizes the hapax legomenon lenidah from the root nud, meaning an object of head-shaking or scorn, though many scholars take it as an orthographic variant of niddah, an unclean or impure thing as in 1:17, matching the purity imagery of 1:8-9.
notes.1:12: Literally "not to you," an elliptical Hebrew expression commonly understood as a rhetorical question, "Is it nothing to you?" or as a wish, "May this not happen to you."
notes.1:13: The difficult Masoretic form wayyirdennah is parsed here as Qal wayyiqtol 3ms of radah or radad ("subdue, master, prevail over") with a 3fs suffix referring collectively to the bones, rather than emending to Hiphil of yarad ("made it descend").
notes.1:14: The hapax legomenon nisqad (Niphal perfect 3ms) is understood from context and Aramaic/rabbinic cognates as "was bound on" or "fastened," matching the imagery of a yoke and intertwined cords.
notes.1:21: The verb hebeta is literally a Hiphil perfect 2ms ("You have brought"), referring to the day of judgment already brought upon Zion; many grammarians also note it may function as a precative perfect ("Bring the day You announced").
notes.2:1: The hapax legomenon yaib is a Hiphil imperfect 3ms of a denominative verb from ab ("cloud"), meaning to cover or shroud with a cloud, used poetically for past action after the lament exclamation "How."
notes.2:13: Following MT aidk (Hiphil imperfect 1cs with 2fs suffix of ud, "testify, cite as witness"), asking what witness or precedent can be adduced to console Jerusalem.
notes.2:14: Translates the Qere shebutek in the idiom heshib shebut ("restore fortunes"); the Ketiv reads shebitek ("your captivity," i.e., "turn back your captivity").
notes.2:18: Following MT strictly (Qal perfect 3ms with 3mp suffix on "heart," referring to the people of Zion), before the poem abruptly shifts to direct address of the wall of the daughter of Zion.
notes.3:10: The ketiv and qere are alternate Hebrew forms for "lion" (aryeh vs. ari) with no difference in meaning.
notes.3:13: "The sons of His quiver" is a literal Hebrew poetic idiom for arrows, and "kidneys" denotes the innermost vitals.
notes.3:17: The Qal verb can be parsed as either second-person masculine singular ("You have rejected my soul from peace") or third-person feminine singular ("my soul has been estranged from peace"). Because Qal zanach is regularly transitive with God as subject (cf. 3:31), it is translated here as a direct address to God.
notes.3:20: The qere reads a Qal third-person feminine singular verb ("sinks down") with "my soul" as subject of both verbs; the ketiv consonants can be read either as Qal from a verb meaning "broods/complains" or as Hiphil ("brings down").
notes.3:26: The Hebrew clause is terse, literally "good, both waiting and in silence," pairing a verbal adjective for waiting with an adverb meaning silently.
notes.3:36: Literally "the Lord has not seen," using the verb raah in the sense of looking favorably upon or approving; some alternatively take it as a rhetorical question ("does the Lord not see?").
notes.3:41: The preposition el ("to") is used here in the sense of al ("together with" or "upon"), picturing lifting the heart together with upturned hands in prayer.
notes.3:51: The Poel verb olalah ("deals harshly with" or "torments") is used elsewhere in Lamentations for severe affliction (1:12, 22; 2:20), and the preposition min is causal ("because of").
notes.3:56: The rare noun ravchati ("my gasping" or "my relief," cf. Exod 8:11) derives from a root meaning "breathe freely" or "find relief"; paired with "my cry for help" after "Your ear," it denotes either a desperate gasp for breath or an appeal for relief.
notes.3:65: The rare construct phrase meginnat-lev literally means "a covering of heart" (from a root meaning "cover" or "shield"), denoting obstinacy or dullness of heart; some alternatively connect it to a root meaning "anguish."
notes.4:3: Ketiv/Qere variants: the Qere reads tannim ("jackals," standard Hebrew plural agreeing with the plural verbs) against the Ketiv tannin (an Aramaizing plural or singular "sea monster"), and reads the single-word Qere kay'enim ("like ostriches") where the Ketiv splits the consonants into two words.
notes.4:6: The nouns for "iniquity" and "sin" here encompass both guilt and its resulting punishment. The clause "and no hands fell upon her" renders the Qal perfect of hul ("whirl/fall upon"), contrasting Sodom's sudden overthrow with Jerusalem's prolonged siege.
notes.4:12: Ketiv/Qere variant: the Qere omits the conjunction before "all" (kol), translated asyndetically, whereas the Ketiv reads "and all" (wkol).
notes.4:17: Ketiv/Qere variant: the Qere reads odenu (first-person plural, "still we"), whereas the Ketiv reads an archaic/adverbial form odynh ("still/yet").
notes.4:22: Hebrew awon ("iniquity") denotes both guilt and the penalty it brings. The verse also plays on two stems of the root glh: Hiphil lehaglotek ("send you into exile") for Zion and Piel gillah ("lay bare") for Edom.
notes.5:5: The MT reads al tsawwarenu nirdaphnu (preposition al with Niphal perfect of rdp, literally "upon our neck we are pursued"), an idiom for relentless pursuit hard at one's heels. The Qere also adds the conjunction "and" before "no" (wlo; Ketiv lo).
notes.5:7: Ketiv/Qere variants: the Qere supplies the conjunction ("and/yet") before both enam ("they are gone") and anahnu ("we"), sharpening the contrast between the fathers' sin and the survivors' burden.
notes.5:12: Hebrew beyadam (literally "by their hand") can mean either that princes were hanged by the enemies' hand or that they were hung up by their own hands.
notes.5:21: Ketiv/Qere variant: following the Hiphil imperative hashibenu ("bring us back"), the Qere reads the Qal cohortative wnashubah ("that we may return"), whereas the Ketiv reads the simple Qal imperfect wnashub ("and we will return").
notes.5:22: The opening conjunction ki im is a noted crux in Biblical Hebrew and can be read as "unless" (qualifying the petition of v. 21), "for surely," or "even though."

unplaced.text: It is by the steadfast kindnesses of the LORD that we have not perished, because His compassions are not exhausted.
unplaced.note: Follows the Masoretic Hebrew first-person plural verb rather than the third-person emendation adopted by some ancient versions.

unplaced.text: They are fresh each morning; abundant is Your faithfulness.
"My portion is the LORD," my soul has said; therefore I will hope in Him.
Let him place his mouth in the dust—perhaps there is hope.
